messages.subject: poppr version 2.0.0 released on CRAN
messages.body_plain:
poppr version 2.0.0 has been released

Here's a link to the details of all the changes for this release <https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/releases/tag/v.2.0.0>.

Note: It might take a day or two for the windows and OSX versions to build. You can check the status by going to http://cran.r-project.org/package=poppr

This version implements all of the features described in our Frontiers paper that was released in June <http://journal.frontiersin.org/article/10.3389/fgene.2015.00208/full>. It also implements changes that were a result of a Population Genetics in R hackathon at NESCent in March of 2015 <https://github.com/NESCent/r-popgen-hackathon>, where major changes happened to the adegenet package <https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet>. Many of the changes helped improved the stability and efficiency of both poppr and adegenet.

This version of poppr contains breaking changes. Please read this vignette for details on those changes <http://cran.rstudio.com/web/packages/poppr/vignettes/how_to_migrate.pdf>. If you have questions after reading the vignette, please post to this forum so others can find the solutions.

Major (breaking) Changes:
The genind/genclone objects are now half their original size
The "hierarchy" slot from genclone objects (poppr) have been moved to genind objects (adegenet) and renamed to "strata"
The function splitcombine has been removed
New Features (highlights):
Multilocus genotype definitions can be changed with the mlg.filter and mll.custom functions (read the vignette on MLGs) <http://cran.rstudio.com/web/packages/poppr/vignettes/mlg.html>
The new object snpclone allows you to perform multilocus genotype analysis on SNP data (inherited from genlight objects)
Sliding window analysis of the index of association
Add reticulations to minimum spanning networks with the option include.ties = TRUE in poppr.msn and bruvo.msn
Interactive Minimum Spanning Network construction with the function imsn (view an example on github <https://github.com/zkamvar/poppr_msn_shiny>)
Cheers,
Zhian N. Kamvar

messages.subject: Re: poppr::info_table with recoded data
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I realized I had replied to Federico only and not the group in general. Recoded data should work in poppr version 2.0. The previous version 1.1 simply would attempt to count the zero alleles present in the data to avoid rounding errors. Since the new version of adegenet represents data as counts of alleles instead of frequencies, the calculation has become simpler as reporting the number of observed alleles. In version 2.0, the following code will work:

pltr <- info_table(iPinf, type = "ploidy", plot = TRUE)
#
# Assign ploidy of samples based on highest observed
(iPinfn <- recode_polyploids(Pinf, newploidy = TRUE))
#
# This is a genclone object
# -------------------------
#   Genotype information:
#
#   72 multilocus genotypes
#   86 triploid (55) and diploid (31) individuals
#   11 codominant loci
#
# Population information:
#
#   2 strata - Continent Country
#   2 populations defined - South America North America
pltrn <- info_table(iPinfn, type = "ploidy", plot = TRUE)
#
# Both can go back
recode_polyploids(iPinf, addzero = TRUE)
#
# This is a genclone object
# -------------------------
#   Genotype information:
#
#   72 original multilocus genotypes
#   86 tetraploid individuals
#   11 codominant loci
#
# Population information:
#
#   2 strata - Continent Country
#   2 populations defined - South America North America
#
recode_polyploids(iPinfn, addzero = TRUE)
#
# This is a genclone object
# -------------------------
#   Genotype information:
#
#   72 original multilocus genotypes
#   86 triploid individuals
#   11 codominant loci
#
# Population information:
#
#   2 strata - Continent Country
#   2 populations defined - South America North America

Hope that helps!
Zhian

On Friday, June 12, 2015 at 10:09:21 AM UTC-7, Federico Urban wrote:
>
>
> Since the info_table function is pretty valid for displaying ploidy I've tried to use it with recoded data with the following commands
>
> data(Pinf)
>
> iPinf <- recode_polyploids(Pinf)
>
> info_table(iPinf, type = "ploidy", plot = TRUE, low = "black", high = "orange")
>
> this will produce the following error:
>
> Error: test_zeroes(x) is not TRUE
>
> How to fix this?
>
>
> The fact that I'm using ploidy analysis with recoded data is because the original data will present zeros that are not real allele information but missing information.
>
> Many thanks for who can help me.
>
> Federico

messages.subject_clean: [Bug Report] Re: poppr version 2.0.0 released on CRAN
messages.body_plain:
Bug report 2015-07-13:

A bug was discovered in read.genalex that prevented missing data from being
imported. A fix was written and will be uploaded soon. In the meantime, please use
the source code at https://gist.github.com/zkamvar/b64078a0d04d2452c905

Below is an example of how to install the fix within R:

library("poppr")
data(nancycats)
outfile <- tempfile()
genind2genalex(nancycats, outfile)

## Extracting the table ... Writing the table to /var/folders/qd/dpdhfsz12wb3c7wz0xdm6dbm0000gn/T//RtmpGojara/file262234cd650e ... Done.

summary(read.genalex(outfile)) # no missing data!

##
##  # Total number of genotypes:  237
##
##  # Population sample sizes:
## P01 P02 P03 P04 P05 P06 P07 P08 P09 P10 P11 P12 P13 P14 P15 P16 P17
##  10  22  12  23  15  11  14  10   9  11  20  14  13  17  11  12  13
##
##  # Number of alleles per locus:
##  fca8 fca23 fca43 fca45 fca77 fca78 fca90 fca96 fca37
##    16    11    10     9    12     8    12    12    18
##
##  # Number of alleles per population:
## P01 P02 P03 P04 P05 P06 P07 P08 P09 P10 P11 P12 P13 P14 P15 P16 P17
##  36  53  50  67  48  56  42  54  43  46  70  52  44  61  42  40  35
##
##  # Percentage of missing data:
## [1] 2.344116
##
##  # Observed heterozygosity:
##      fca8     fca23     fca43     fca45     fca77     fca78     fca90
## 0.6682028 0.6666667 0.6793249 0.7083333 0.6329114 0.5654008 0.6497890
##     fca96     fca37
## 0.6184211 0.4514768
##
##  # Expected heterozygosity:
##      fca8     fca23     fca43     fca45     fca77     fca78     fca90
## 0.8657224 0.7928751 0.7953319 0.7603095 0.8702576 0.6884669 0.8157881
##     fca96     fca37
## 0.7603493 0.6062686

Installing the fix (should use devtools):

devtools::source_gist("https://gist.github.com/zkamvar/b64078a0d04d2452c905",
                      sha1 = "74ff482c9832237092ffb29a5955ee68b255005f")

## Sourcing https://gist.githubusercontent.com/zkamvar/b64078a0d04d2452c905/raw/62ba9500d8fdaa09b0b520a45d2b04ebb44d6940/poppr_patches.R
##
## fixing function 'read.genalex' ...
##
## Everything is up to date!
both_identical <- identical(summary(read.genalex(outfile), verbose = FALSE), summary(nancycats, verbose = FALSE))
both_identical

## [1] TRUE

I apologize any inconvenience this may have caused anyone

Cheers,
Zhian

messages.subject: probelm with missing data when using the function read.genalex
messages.subject_clean: probelm with missing data when using the function read.genalex
messages.body_plain:
Dear poppr users,

I recently start to use the poppr package as I found very appealing the possibility to create genind objects by using as input files .csv created in genAlex.
I created a .csv file (attached) consisting of microsatellites data on 95 populations surveyed at 4 loci. Alleles have 3-digit code. Missing data are scored as "0" (as genAlex tutorial suggest to score missing data).

The problem arise when I try to load the input file in poppr using the line DATA=read.genalex (filename, quiet=T)
When I run the function info_table(DATA) to check for number of missing data, the function reports that there are none (indeed, after checking, the zero values are replaced with "NA" when the file is imported).

I don't know where the problem lies. I checked whether the file was properly comma delimited and it looks like. I also tried to export the "nancycats" dataset included in the package adegenet as genAlex using the function genind2genalex, and then importing this newly created .cvs files back into R with the read.genalex function. Well..the missing data present in the nancycats genind object are not there anymore if I import it with the read.genalex function.
It appears there is something wrong in the way the genind object code the missing data when the input file is loaded with the read.genalex function.
Or it might be a more trivial problem, due to my incapability of seeing a very simple mistake in my file.

I would be really glad if someone could help me with this issue.

Thanks in advance for your time

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

We caught the bug at the same time, it appears <https://groups.google.com/d/msg/poppr/KBJ7TjQolj0/aPiA3BxrEw0J>. I have fixed it on the master branch of the github repository. I have also posted a patch at https://gist.github.com/zkamvar/b64078a0d04d2452c905

You can either download it and use source("poppr_patches.R") or you can use devtools to install directly from the internet:

devtools::source_gist("https://gist.github.com/zkamvar/b64078a0d04d2452c905",
                      sha1 = "74ff482c9832237092ffb29a5955ee68b255005f")

You can also install the development version if you have a C compiler:

devtools::install_github("grunwaldlab/poppr")

I'm sorry for the inconvenience. Hope that helps!

Cheers,
Zhian

I would like change the limits to enable the comparison of both populations by concurrently inspecting the heat maps. In my case, I would like the color limits to be (0, 15). Is this possible?

While the code was predominantly used from pegas, I wanted to know if there were modifications in your code that may produce such results? I have conducted HWE tests in Genalex and Arlequin and the results are not all equal to 1.

Many thanks,
Genevieve

messages.subject: Re: Changing limits of color ramp for % missing data produced by info_table
messages.subject_clean: Changing limits of color ramp for % missing data produced by info_table
messages.body_plain:
Hi Genevieve,

>
> 1) info_table function. I would like to change the limits on the color ramp for percent missing data. Currently they are set at 0 - the observed maximum percent missing data, or 0-100%. I would like change the limits to enable the comparison of both populations by concurrently inspecting the heat maps. In my case, I would like the color limits to be (0, 15). Is this possible?

This is possible. The only drawback is that anything above the limit will display as grey by default. Here's an example with the monpop dataset, which has a maximum of 7.6% missing data:

library("poppr")
library("ggplot2")
data("monpop")
info_table(monpop, type = "missing", plot = TRUE) # Defaults to (0, max)
monplot <- last_plot() # grab last plot from ggplot2
# setting the limits to a max of 5% in blue and yellow and displaying anything higher as red (the default would be grey)
monplot + scale_fill_gradient(low = "blue", high = "yellow", na.value = "red", limits = c(0, 5))

> 2) The population level HWE test I am running produces an expected heterozygosity of 1 for all populations. While the code was predominantly used from pegas, I wanted to know if there were modifications in your code that may produce such results? I have conducted HWE tests in Genalex and Arlequin and the results are not all equal to 1.

There are many things that could be going on here. Are you using hw.test from pegas? Do you have polyploid data? What version of poppr are you using?

Cheers,
Zhian

messages.body_plain:
Hi Genevieve,

I apologize for the lateness of my reply. I realized one thing: you asked about expected heterozygosity, yet hw.test in pegas does not report that. It simply reports the results of a chi^2 test.

My hunch is that you might have gotten the value from the function called poppr().

My reasoning for that is that the poppr function returns a table of multilocus genotypic diversity. One of the diversity measures in version 1.x.x was called Hexp and described as expected heterozygosity, but this was not so. In reality, it was an unbiased Simpson's diversity measure. Since this was calculated on multilocus genotype counts, sexual populations would have Hexp reported as 1 (I had attempted to fix it in poppr version 2.0, but I have just discovered that there is a bug in that specific calculation for which I will post a fix momentarily). Might this be the reason you are seeing 1 for this value?

Cheers,
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: poppr 2.0.1 released on CRAN
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

It appears there is a small numerical bug in the calculation of Hexp (from the functions poppr and locus_table). I cannot upload a new version to CRAN for another couple of weeks, so until then please use the following code every time you load poppr:

devtools::source_gist("b64078a0d04d2452c905")

You can also download the code from here: https://gist.github.com/zkamvar/b64078a0d04d2452c905

If you have a C compiler on your computer, you may also install directly from GitHub:

devtools::install_github("grunwaldlab/poppr")

Details on the change can be found here: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/issues/47

Sorry for the inconvenience,
Zhian
